comparator.academicYear: Current prospective curriculum pages checked 2026-09-25 (concurrent year overviews)
comparator.route: General Politicologie bachelor with open third-year choice
comparator.sourceNotes: The official prospective year pages total 60+60+60=180 EC. Years one and two each list ten 6-EC compulsory political-science courses, including methods, statistics, two second-year projects and international/conflict study. Year three lists 6 EC Politics, Ethics and Practice, 6 EC International Relations in the Indo-Pacific, one 6-EC choice between democracy-under-pressure and borders/migration options, 30 EC genuine minor/elective/internship space and a required 12-EC bachelor thesis. The year-two page spells “Qualtitative”; the source name is retained verbatim in the comparator. Third-year named electives and thesis themes are choices, not all compulsory. Prospectus year pages show concurrent cohorts and are not a guarantee of a single entrant-cohort three-year timetable.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Two distinct feasible UCR pathways cover the broad political-science core and an international-conflict focus. A third democracy, social justice or political-theory proposal would mostly rearrange the same small UCR politics, law and sociology catalogue and lacks four course changes backed by a distinct political-science sequence.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Introduces comparative political institutions and concepts.
The related UCR course is already assigned to another distinct comparator component; this requirement remains separately visible.
Both examine European integration and EU politics.
No scheduled dedicated course on parties as organisations with historical development.
Both address power and identity; UCR takes a social-theory perspective.
Both address political thought; UCR introduces the field rather than surveying its full history.
The related UCR course is already assigned to another distinct comparator component; this requirement remains separately visible.
Both examine rights and justice, through different law-and-philosophy and political-science approaches.
Student selects one advanced politics option; neither particular topic is universal.
Both examine political conflict; UCR is an advanced peace-and-conflict course.
Both consider international organisation and cooperation through different emphases.
Both address political violence and war; UCR teaches military history, not conflict-transformation practice.
No scheduled course directly represents the separately credited global political-economy requirement.
Both address EU institutions and external rules; UCR is a law course and does not reproduce the Radboud group project.
No dedicated changing-world foreign-policy analysis course among the selected UCR courses.
Both develop ethical reasoning, though UCR has general ethics rather than political practice.
UCR offers international relations and conflict but no dedicated Indo-Pacific political-science case course.
Both introduce empirical research design and methods; UCR is cross-disciplinary.
Both develop academic argument and communication through different contexts.
Radboud requires dedicated statistics for political scientists; a cross-disciplinary introductory methods course is already paired with research design and cannot substitute twice.
No separately scheduled advanced quantitative political-science methods course.
Both introduce qualitative empirical methods, with UCR taught in sociology.
No corresponding supervised political-science democracy-and-conflict project.
Thirty EC of minor, elective or placement space is truly student-selected and has no single course equivalent.
Radboud requires an independent political-science bachelor thesis; UCR course work does not individually replace it.

notes.text: UCR offers substantive comparative politics, political theory, international relations, peace and conflict, EU law, sociology and cross-disciplinary research methods. Radboud requires a denser political-science methods curriculum, two project courses and a 12-EC discipline-specific thesis. UCR alternatives illustrate related programmes, without implying equivalent credits, political-science qualification or admission guarantees.
